title: Review docs/design/job-planning.md against the code
summary: Write an independent review of docs/design/job-planning.md in the existing review format, checking its (read) code claims against the code, the section 8 job ordering and sizing, and the section 9 keep rule. Only the review file and CHANGELOG.md change; it ends with a verdict.

defaults_applied.how: Every finding cites file and line or a record; unmeasured numbers labeled estimates.
Review written for an outside reader, without naming the operator or host.
No secrets or personal data; avoids words the boundary test rejects.
Code claims checked against actual lines, not existence.
cargo fmt --check and cargo test run by verifier.
BRIEF.md asks for tagged releases and a changelog, so the change records itself in CHANGELOG.md.

assumptions: Audience is Sri and the build-job verifier; goal is an independent, evidence-cited review ahead of building the design.
The reviewed commit is the one checked out when the producer runs; it records its hash.
Existing reviews in docs/design/reviews/ define the format; producer reads them first.
Design is docs-class work; no code or governance files change.

acceptance_criteria.text: docs/design/reviews/job-planning-review-1.md exists, names the reviewed commit, and follows the format of existing reviews in docs/design/reviews/ (severity High/Medium/Low, evidence, proposed fix per finding).
For each of the design's sections 3 to 9 the review lists findings or states it has none; every finding has severity, evidence (file:line or record) and a proposed fix.

Each (read) code claim in the design that was checked (run.rs dispatch and produce_and_verify, manage.rs recover_interrupted, store.rs job_of, admission::is_governance, governance_change_is_listed, athena_agent::policy::evaluate, Config::validate, verify::judge) is listed as confirmed or contradicted with the line checked.
The review assesses section 8's five build jobs for ordering (no config change before its schema) and single-producer-run fit, and whether section 9's keep rule is computable from Athena's records.
The review ends with a verdict: build as designed, build after the listed fixes, or redesign.
The review does not name who runs Athena or where (boundary test in xtask/tests/policy.rs); the design file and code are unchanged.
Run cargo fmt --check and cargo test: both pass, including the xtask policy boundary test; git status shows only the review file and CHANGELOG.md changed.
CHANGELOG.md has an entry for the review.

out_of_scope: Changing any code, tests, or configuration
departures: Review needs reading many code files against the design, so cost and time sit above the reference; boundary-word test adds failure risk.
